The Architecture of Custody

The Contagion of Distrust: Rootstock Staggers as Liquid Panic Spreads Across Bitcoin Sidechains

By 21 Milioni di Chiacchiere & Staff

Following the $320M Elements cache exploit, depositors rush to exit Bitcoin sidechains, triggering a 46-hour peg-out backlog on Rootstock and forcing a reckoning with the fragile assumptions between layers.

The fallout from the 4,000 BTC drainage of the Liquid Network is no longer confined to Blockstream’s federated sidechain. In the twenty-four hours since an incomplete cache key permitted unauthorized peg-outs against the federation’s reserves, a run on secondary layers has spread across the Bitcoin ecosystem. As depositors rushed to reclaim base-layer satoshis, Rootstock—a merge-mined sidechain utilizing a PowPeg architecture—began reporting severe delays of nearly two days for users attempting to withdraw funds.

Writing in an extensive architectural analysis, 21 Milioni di Chiacchiere observed that L'hack di Liquid ha aperto una crepa che va ben oltre Liquid. Users attempting to escape potential vulnerabilities quickly overwhelmed the peg infrastructure: Gli utenti stanno abbandonando un'altra side chain, Rootstock, che adesso ha ritardi 36-46 ore nei peg-out, causati da un esaurimento temporaneo dell'inventario UTXO del PowPeg per un'ondata di prelievi simultanei.

The root problem is not a defect in Bitcoin itself, which processed transactions without interruption. Rather, as sidechain bridges and wrapped representations proliferate, depositors are being confronted with the reality that an asset locked in a secondary protocol carries the cumulative risk of every intermediary component: smart contracts, hardware security modules, and federation keys. As 21 Milioni di Chiacchiere noted, la sicurezza di Bitcoin non si trasferisce automaticamente a tutto ciò che costruisce un ponte verso Bitcoin.

Reflecting on the crisis, Phaedrus pointed out the defining contrast with account-based networks: So far it looks like nobody has the power to revert (unlike Ethereum). While Ethereum famously executed a state rollback following the DAO exploit a decade ago, Bitcoin base-layer miners and nodes continue to enforce consensus without intervention, leaving the sidechains to absorb the full reputational and economic shock.

Classroom Frontiers

Thirty Students Cross the Threshold: Bitcoin Classroom Expands in Thailand

Dispatch by Jimmy Kostro

At the Bitcoin Learning Center, international high schoolers encounter sound money outside the commercial banking system.

While global infrastructure grappled with institutional sidechain failures, circular adoption continued at a human scale in Southeast Asia. Jimmy Kostro hosted an international high school class at the Bitcoin Learning Center in Thailand. Reflecting on the visit, he wrote: Today an International Highschool brought their students to the Bitcoin Learning Center, here in Thailand. Often I can not believe we get to experience all of this.

In a second transmission filing the classroom photograph, Kostro recorded the milestone with characteristic brevity: The network grew by 30 students today.

Special Dispatch

“Bebe Did Exactly What She Was Built to Do”

GlobalTraces in Kazakhstan

Five years on the road end in a rollover at a half-finished toll booth.

For six years, Dave, Jess, Isla, and Otis poured their life savings into a customized expedition truck named Bebe, turning her into an off-grid home, mobile school, and office. A few weeks ago in Kazakhstan, Bebe’s front tire struck an unmarked concrete plinth at an unlit toll booth, blowing both tires and flipping the vehicle onto its side.

In a dispatch published after hospital discharge, Dave shared his young daughter’s raw reaction: Why did Bebe have to hurt herself to keep us safe? It wasn’t her job.

The family escaped with concussions, whiplash, and bruises, but the truck’s habitation box and chassis were ruined: Bebe, our home for the last five years, has been catastrophically damaged. Without commercial overland insurance available outside Europe, the community has rallied to support their journey back to England. Read the full dispatch on Jumble.

Decentralized Engineering

Forge-Free Code: ngit v3 and GitWorkshop v4 Bring CI to Nostr

Report by DanConwayDev

Self-hosted continuous integration and microVM job runners arrive over NIP-34.

A sovereign network requires sovereign developer tooling. DanConwayDev announced the simultaneous release of ngit v3 and GitWorkshop v4, describing the milestone as The biggest release yet brings CI, private repositories, forge-free software releases and much more.

Powered by the Grasp backend, the release introduces ngit-ci 0.1, a coordinator capable of executing containerized CI pipelines and microVM testing without centralized platforms like GitHub Actions.

Sovereign Systems

Umbrel Lightning Nodes Gain Isolated Keys; Bitfest 2026 Set

Protocol & Community Wire

Announcing a self-custody Zap and Nostr Wallet Connect client for Umbrel node runners, ⚡ Dee Kay ⚡ articulated the bedrock security philosophy of relay architecture: Relays are transport, not trust. By generating isolated Nostr keys on the node hardware and encrypting payloads via NIP-44, so a relay only ever carries signed, encrypted payloads it cannot read or forge.

In the UK, Aaron of Essex announced Bitfest 2026, taking place November 19–22 in Manchester across nine themed zones. Day zero will launch Nostrshire, the country’s first dedicated Nostr conference. Why gather in person? As Aaron noted, the conversations in hallways and over coffee are where real collaborations start.
